subject: Dedicated capacity: burst conditioning & session conductivity
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex@civicmind.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated fleet question — burst conductivity and latency under session multiplexing

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this — quick background: CivicMind runs a user-facing conversational API (SaaS) that mixes short assistant completions (30–80 token prompts) with occasional long-generation workflows (responses up to ~450 tokens). We get steady baseline traffic but have short, hard bursts when a campaign or event triggers many parallel sessions. Bursts are:
- peak requests: ~500-700 reqs/min for 3–7 minutes (occurs ~2–3x/day)
- median concurrent sessions during burst: ~220
- typical prompt length: 45–70 tokens, 95th percentile response length: 380–480 tokens

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated and want to understand:
1) How you account for "burst conductivity" — i.e., how spikes propagate between session pools when sessions are sharded across GPUs and how that affects tail latency.
2) What telemetry / sample data you need from us to size reserved capacity (concurrency, token histogram, dayparting).
3) Any recommended headroom multiplier for our workload (we've seen P99 latency blow up under 4x median concurrency).

Attached: civicmind_traffic_sample.csv (5 days sample) and short prompt_response_samples.jsonl (10 examples) — please treat as internal only.

Looking for a short sketch to help our infra lead prep for an exec review next week.

Best,
Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform
CivicMind

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Moreno <alex@civicmind.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated fleet question — burst conductivity and latency under session multiplexing

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the sample files. Quick clarifying q's before we sketch a capacity profile: 

- Is the burst arrival shape spiky (many requests in <30s) or ramped over several minutes? You noted 3–7 minutes — is there a consistent front-loaded spike?
- Are requests pinned to user sessions (long lived) or stateless ephemeral calls from many clients? That affects our session affinity recommendations.
- Do you use streaming (chunked) responses for the long generations? If so, p50/p95 chunk sizes help.

What we'll produce after those answers: a short sketch including recommended reserved GPU count (by SKU), concurrency targets per GPU, suggested KV-cache share & prefix caching, and a 95/99 latency projection with 1.25/1.5 headroom options.

Next steps: if you can confirm the three bullets and drop a 24h token histogram for a high-traffic day, I'll pull Karthik in to run a quick load model. We can also do a 30-min sync — link below.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On Sat, May 29, 2027 at 10:05 AM Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the sample files. Quick clarifying q's before we sketch a capacity profile: 
> 
> - Is the burst arrival shape spiky (many requests in <30s) or ramped over several minutes? You noted 3–7 minutes — is there a consistent front-loaded spike?
> - Are requests pinned to user sessions (long lived) or stateless ephemeral calls from many clients? That affects our session affinity recommendations.
> - Do you use streaming (chunked) responses for the long generations? If so, p50/p95 chunk sizes help.

Answers: 
- Burst shape: usually front-loaded — ~60% of the burst volume hits in the first 45–60s, then decays over 4–6 minutes. Occasionally a micro-spike (<30s) occurs during a campaign start.
- Sessions: mixed. 70% are short-lived (single-call), 30% are session-bound (conversation stickiness ~10–40 minutes).
- Streaming: yes for the long generations — we stream in ~2–3 chunks typically; p95 chunk ~150 tokens.

Attached a one-day token histogram and a 24h arrival-rate CSV (named civicmind_traffic_sample.csv) — the sample includes timestamps, token_in, token_out, session_id.

We'd love a sketch this week. We're targeting an internal exec sync on Thu; if you can get something by Wed EOD that'd be ideal.

Cheers,
Alex

Attachments: civicmind_traffic_sample.csv, prompt_response_samples.jsonl

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.inference>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated fleet question — burst conductivity and latency under session multiplexing

Folks — forwarding CivicMind's traffic sample and answers. Quick take: front-loaded spikes + mix of session types — classic case where aggressive prefix caching and a modest over-provision buffer improves P99 without doubling cost.

Proposed immediate plan (sketch for Wed deliverable):
- Run our ranker: feed the CSV into the sizing tool with these scenarios: baseline (no headroom), +25% headroom, +50% headroom; simulate with 2 GPU SKUs: L40s-80 and A100-80.
- Quantization plan: test 4-bit QAT path for long-gen models (saves ~28% tokens/sec cost) but keep unquantized for low-latency short paths.
- Session affinity: recommend sticky sessions for the 30% session-bound traffic using soft-pinning to reduce KV cache churn.
- Fallback: define a canary fallback policy to a smaller model variant for sustained overloads >5 minutes.

Can Karthik run the sizing sim Monday morning and we draft the slide sketch by Tue? Marissa — can you add latency targets (p50/p95/p99) for the customer-facing SLOs and call out acceptable tail tradeoffs? I'll assemble a 1-slide summary + a 1-page ops playbook for Wed.

Thanks —
Jordan
